name: TensorRT-LLM: Llama 3.3 70B FP8 on 2x H100 SXM 80GB (TP=2), ISL/OSL 1000/2000
methodology: TensorRT-LLM PyTorch backend, trtllm-bench throughput. Hardware: 2x NVIDIA H100 SXM 80GB (DGX H100), tensor-parallel size = 2, pipeline parallel 1. ISL = 1000, OSL = 2000, uniform synthetic dataset, 1500 requests. Concurrency not fixed: offline infinite-rate load, achieved in-flight batch omitted by the source. Figure is AGGREGATE output tokens/s summed over the 2-GPU TP group (about 1854 tok/s per GPU). KV cache free-memory fraction 0.95; CUDA graphs enabled for batch sizes 1-8192.
notes: Measured by NVIDIA, published in the TensorRT-LLM performance overview and reproducible with the documented `prepare_dataset.py` + `trtllm-bench throughput --backend pytorch` workflow (llm_options.yml with CUDA-graph batch sizes 1..8192, kv_cache_free_gpu_mem_fraction 0.95). Metric is 'Total Output Throughput (tokens/sec)' as trtllm-bench reports it: AGGREGATE output tokens/s across all in-flight requests at the stated TP size, under an offline infinite-rate request feed, NOT per-request and NOT per-GPU. Model weights are NVIDIA-published ModelOpt-quantized checkpoints. The page explicitly states these are reference points, not peak performance, and that batch size / parallelism were left mostly at defaults.
